title: Family mourns a gentle father: Depressed Stittsville man shot dead by police
article: A Stittsville man shot dead by police last week after he stabbed his wife in a rage was remembered yesterday as a gentle father who adored his wife.
Family and friends of Frank Hutterer, 35, gathered at a quiet Unitarian funeral service here to praise a kind-hearted man who suddenly turned violent.
"Sally, the day you and Frank met you were a very special couple," Dave Hutterer, Frank's brother, said during a eulogy at the Rod Abram's Funeral Home.
"He often told me how much he loved you and how good you were to him."

Yesterday, Sally McIntyre, 34, wept silently beside her son during a memorial service while many struggled to understand what went wrong. The only sign of the physical trauma she suffered was heavy gauze on her right hand.
Those close to the couple say Mr. Hutterer's attack on his wife last Wednesday was completely out of character.

For years, he battled depression. Last week, in a state of despair, Mr. Hutterer went to the emergency room at the Royal Ottawa Hospital. A doctor there examined Mr. Hutterer and recommended that he check himself in, but he went home.
The next day, Mr. Hutterer lost control of himself and became possessed with rage.
As Ms. McIntyre readied her son for school, Mr. Hutterer confronted her, attacking his wife with two butcher knives.
When police arrived, Mr. Hutterer lunged at a female officer with his knives. She shot him, but he continued toward her. She shot him three more times, killing him.
